title: Repeat Within K Positions
statement:
You get an integer array nums and an integer k. Return true if some value appears at two different indexes i and j with |i − j| ≤ k, and false otherwise.

A repeat that is further apart than k does not count.

examples.why: The two 4s are at indexes 0 and 3: exactly 3 apart, and the limit is inclusive.
Same repeat, but now 3 is more than the allowed 2.
Both values repeat, but each repeat is 2 apart. Just checking "is there any duplicate" says true here, which is wrong.

hints: For each position you only care about the k positions right before it. What do you need to remember about them?
Keep the last k values in a set, like a sliding window. If the current value is already in the set, you have a close repeat.
After checking position i, add nums[i] and, once the window holds more than k values, remove nums[i − k]. Alternatively, store each value's last index in a map and compare distances.

explain.intuition:
For every index, the only partners that matter are the k indexes right before it. Anything earlier is too far, and anything later will check against this one when its own turn comes. So slide a window of the last k values along the array, and keep them in a set for O(1) lookups.

An equivalent view: remember the last index each value was seen at. The nearest earlier copy is the best possible partner, so you only need to compare against it. This is the same idea as a debounce: only the most recent event matters for deciding whether the new one is "too close".
steps: For each index i: if nums[i] is in the set, return true.
If the set now has more than k values, remove nums[i − k], the value that just fell out of range.
pitfalls: Checking for any duplicate at all and ignoring the distance, as in the third example.
An off-by-one in the window size, which turns "at most k apart" into "less than k apart".
With the map version, keeping the first index of a value instead of the latest. The latest one is always the closest to whatever comes next.

solutions.title: Check the previous k for every index
solutions.idea: For each index, compare it with the up to k indexes before it.

solutions.title: Last index per value
solutions.idea: Remember where each value was last seen; a repeat is close enough if it is within k of that index.

solutions.title: Sliding window set
solutions.idea: Keep exactly the last k values in a set. A value already in the set is a repeat within range.

followups: Instead of equal values, look for two values that differ by at most t and sit at most k apart. Which structure replaces the set?
Count how many such close pairs there are, not just whether one exists.
